agree.reason: The two commissioners focused on traffic hear only that a D grade is a 'slower light,' and nobody tells them the builder will pay for a signal that keeps the intersection at C, so the doubters get little reason to change their votes.

honest.reason: The speech makes claims the facts don't support: 'won't be parking up and down our street,' 'don't have to clear anything or bring in new roads,' and 'a little slower' all go further than the evidence, and it never mentions the existing 8am backups or the 20 months of construction trucks.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out a useful figure (the 64 units would cover about one in six of the families on the waiting list) and notes the eight extra parking spaces, but it leaves out the 2,100-home shortfall in proportion and the signal's effect on the C rating.

right_comparison.reason: It says the alternative is an empty lot and an unchanged waiting list, but it assumes the list stays at 412 without any trend data, and it compares against an unmitigated D rather than a D versus a C with the signal.

qualification.reason: The only condition offered is a vague 'signal-timing review' with no date, number or consequence, when the specific condition available was a builder-funded signal that keeps the intersection at C.

objections.reason: It names the traffic objection but answers it by playing it down instead of with the signal, and it leaves out construction disruption and the weekday parking and neighbour-group commitments that would speak to the opponents in the room.

fit.reason: It is the right form for public comment and roughly fits three minutes at about 430 words, but it still has [Name] and [Church Name] placeholders even though the user gave both names.
